children.name: Blaugust 2026 Recap: Summary From a First Time Participant

summary.value: A review of my first Blaugust event; the pros and cons, what to look forward to next year, and featuring some of the bloggers I enjoyed reading this month.

content.html:
Blaugust 2026 Overview⁠§

Blaugust has motivated me to post the most on any given month of the year (see the trends on the calendar heatmap or monthly spread). But I probably bit off more than I could chew when I announced that I would also join the Community Builder award as a Blaugust first-timer. because in the end, I only managed two of the Community Builder tasks (need a minimum of three to get the award). 😞

Update

James at with words, wonder has given me a chance to guest post on his blog with 15 minutes to spare before the end of August 2026! Here’s a quick note about it.

The guest post is on Chinese Idioms.

Positives⁠§

In terms of how this blogging challenge changed me as a blogger, I think the net result was positive. It gave me a reason to capture fleeting moments, put the experience into words, and publish it quickly; instead of drafting notes that might never be shared.

Then there’s the community aspect of Blaugust which was very inspirational to me. I loved reading posts by other blaug-ers who increased their output for this event, no matter if it was part of the suggested themes/prompts or not.

Negatives⁠§

There have been some negatives though. Throughout the whole month, I felt this invisible pressure of needing to post every day (even though I only set myself the initial goal of 5 or more blog entries).

I know this is just self-inflicted pressure, but it wasn’t that nice. I tend to be my toughest critic and I guess the stress was inevitable. If I had done some basic planning in advance of the challenge (instead of joining last minute) about what blog fodder to develop into posts, I would probably have felt more at ease. Something to think about next year!

Blog Discoveries⁠§

There were just under 160 bloggers who participated in this event! So just like in my Junited 2026 post, I want to highlight some works from blaug-ers I enjoyed reading:

Frances 132 Blaugust postsMichael Harley Please let me interact with your blog post!Ruben Verweij An unconventional photo postJoel @JoelChrono Who am I reading during Blaugust?Jakob @Jak2k The last Monday CommuteJuha-Matti Santala A lot of what I’ve learned, I’ve learned from open webThomas Vander Wal Markdown Apps Loosely Joined@HellraiserMX The not-so-short WireGuard Guide for people getting into Homelabbing.Brennan Kenneth Brown Creating an Open-source Blogging Studies SyllabusAndreas Going viral is kind of scary@Axxuy Writing By HandAriadne No big deal@JCProbably A Year Since the Layoff@Nullish Slow writingTantek Çelik Simple hashtag proposal for dates: datetags for the IndieWebSam @theTangentSpace Workspace and workflowJames G The Poet (Le poète) by PicassoBongo Twisty What might you be resisting?

Closing Thoughts⁠§

Community Builder AwardSilver Core Challenge Award

Although, I failed to meet the Community Builder Award (see update above).

With the last minute guest post on James’s blog, I hit the minimum requirements: 3/5 of the Community Builder Award! I also passed my original goal of +5 posts and managed to muster up 18 entries in total, which means I get the Silver Award (+15 posts)!

Thank you for reading and following along my Blaugust journey! I’ll round up the post by linking to a few other final review posts by other participants:

  • Blaugust 2026 in review | James
  • Blaugust debriefing | What the Fran
  • Now, August 2026: Wrapping up Blaugust and other titbits | Ruben Verweij
  • 31st is for recap | Juha-Matti Santala

That’s it for my Blaugust 2026 recap; see you at the next Blaugust!

—Naty
